selfCorrection.whyItWasWrong: Two errors. First, I conflated 'no owed act' with 'no possible dependent act'. D-137 owes nothing, but a later DR-117 status re-record or SATISFIED-grade application can rely on this recording as its warrant; once one lands, reverting C-D137 alone withdraws the warrant while leaving the dependent live. Second, I cited D-116 as the governing form when it predates the temporal reversibility discipline the corpus established across D-133, D-135 and D-136 — a discipline I had myself endorsed when accepting Codex's D135-SF-2 and when reviewing D-136 turn 3. Citing a pre-discipline precedent as authority against a discipline I had already agreed to is the inconsistency, and it is mine.

substantiveVerification.correctedCount: Nine of fourteen classes are candidate-owned: EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-4, EE-5a, EE-5b, EE-6a, EE-7a and EE-7d. Seven say existingGate 'none' outright; the other two deny a gate in prose rather than by the word — EE-4 reads 'DR-G21 does not own this property' and EE-7a reads 'DR-101 does not own the TypeScript-closure limb of the useful install'. All nine therefore carry no exact DR-G obligation, so nine of fourteen is 'most' and the claim is accurate.
substantiveVerification.gateReasoningChecked: D-056's gate 3 requires the remainder to be already named at a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner, which none of the nine satisfies. Gate 2 requires the remainder to be only execution or measurement, and the pinned D-056 subject excludes authoring from that set — a class with no harness leaves harness authoring outstanding. So both gates are correctly described as unestablished.
